Montana Frost-Free Days

Freeze probabilities and growing-season statistics for Montana, computed from daily station observations, 1991–2025. Built and maintained by Jackson Rose, Geospatial Core Facility, Montana State University.

Definitions. The frost-free period is the span between the last spring freeze and the first fall freeze at the chosen daily-minimum threshold (32, 28, or 24°F); frost-free days count the days strictly between the two freezes. Growing degree days (base 50°F, May–Oct) are a separate quantity. All dates are empirical percentiles over valid years, not fitted distributions: a “cautious” (10%) spring date means only 1 year in 10 froze later. Years with no freeze at a threshold are counted and reported, not dropped; stations need 20+ valid years for full statistics.

Data. Station records: GHCN-Daily via RCC-ACIS (NOAA NCEI). Gridded surface: gridMET ~4 km daily minimum temperature, cross-checked against PRISM monthly normals. Station climatology validated against NOAA 1991–2020 freeze normals (median dates agree within ~3–4 days). Basemaps © OpenStreetMap contributors, © CARTO, Esri.

Honest limits. Statistics belong to stations, not fields: elevation and cold-air drainage dominate Montana freeze timing, and interpolated surfaces at any practical resolution miss cold pools (measured against 505 stations; local seasons can run weeks shorter than the 4 km surface shows). Uncertainty on displayed dates is shown as bootstrap 90% confidence intervals. Seasons have trended ~10 days longer since 2008, so full-window statistics are conservative on the fall side.

Single-file app, no server, generated by a reproducible Python pipeline (pandas, scipy, rasterio, matplotlib; Leaflet for the map). EPSG:4326. v2.0, 2026.
